To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
α2‐Adrenoreceptor‐mediated inhibition of NA release in rat brain is not mediated by a decrease in cAMP levels.
the α2‐agonist BHT‐920 inhibits potassium‐evoked release of NA in rat occipial cortex tissue chops, and this inhibition is not mediated by inhibition of cAMP formation.
α2‐Adrenoceptor agonists, such as clonidine and BHT‐ 920, inhibit the release of noradrenaline from rat occipetal cortex tissue chops.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of α2‐adrenoceptor agonists on noradrenaline release from rat cortical tissue slices, and on cyclic AMP production from slices and homogenates of rat cerebral cortex.
the regulation of noradrenaline (nor‐epinephrine; NA) release in the rat occipital cortical tissue chop preparation.
the regulation of noradrenaline (nor epinephrine) (NA) release from rat occipitocortical tissue chops.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
α2‐Adrenoceptor agonists inhibit noradrenaline release by a mechanism that may not involve cyclic AMP.
the α2‐agonist‐mediated inhibition of NA release in rat cortical tissue is not mediated via a cyclic AMP‐dependent mechanism, but the mechanism of this inhibition remains to be determined.

the α2‐agonists clonidine and BHT‐ 920 inhibit the release of [3‐H]noradrenaline ([3‐H]NA) from rat occipetal cortex tissue slices by a mechanism that is not mediated by the activation of α2‐adrenoceptors coupled to the inhibition or stimulation of adenylate-cyclase.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the inhibitory effects of NA and α2‐adrenoceptor agonists on NA release from rat occipitocortical tissue are not mediated by a reduction in the level of cyclic AMP.
the α2‐agonist inhibition of NA‐release from rat cortical tissue is not mediated by a decrease in cyclic AMP levels.
the α2‐Adrenoceptors in the rat occipital cortices are coupled to the regulation of the release of NA, but not to the formation of cyclic AMP.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the inhibition of NA release by α2‐adrenoceptors is not mediated by inhibition of adenyl cyclase.
the α2‐ARs in the brain are not all alike, and the α2A‐ARs are not the same in the brain as they are in the peripheral tissues, such as the spleen and platelets.
α2‐agonists inhibit NA release in a manner that is not dependent on a decrease in intracellular cyclic AMP levels.
